title: Fresh recovery incarnation and signing-key epoch
description: Objective: mint the non-restored fencing identity that every disaster restore must install. Deliverable: a daemon recovery-incarnation service using the production Node crypto boundary to create a 256-bit CSPRNG nonce and a fresh signing-key epoch, bind both to one backup-generation digest and restore command ID, and return only verification-safe metadata plus protected key material handles. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: RestoreQuiesceWitness carries an arbitrary `recoveryIncarnationRef`, but repo-wide searches find no recovery-incarnation mint, `keyEpoch`, entropy health gate, or restore-key rotation service. NOT in scope: incrementing restored counters, two-slot file installation, session/grant validation, effect inventory, R3 approval, fault fixtures, or persisting raw private keys in events/logs. Hard dependency: task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a defines the backup-generation digest it binds; implementation may plan in parallel but cannot complete against a guessed contract. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.* and minimal daemon export wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: The production service obtains exactly 32 bytes from a CSPRNG and generates a new signing-key epoch outside restored state, returning a frozen versioned binding over restoreCommandId, backupGenerationDigest, incarnation digest/reference, key-epoch reference, and verification-key fingerprint.

Two distinct restore command IDs for the identical backup generation produce distinct incarnation and key-epoch references; no counter, timestamp, backup byte, or caller-selected ID can supply either fresh identity.

Entropy failure, short/randomly repeated output, key-generation failure, or unverifiable public-key metadata refuses with stable `RECOVERY_ENTROPY_UNAVAILABLE` or `RECOVERY_KEY_EPOCH_UNAVAILABLE` at layer `RECOVERY_INCARNATION`, truth `UNKNOWN`, and no prepared authority.

Tests exercise the production crypto adapter, assert no private-key bytes appear in serialized outcomes/errors, pin exact refusal code/layer precedence, and mutation-check the production freshness comparison.

implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED landed and verified red for the RIGHT reason.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run ... src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.test.ts` -> exit 1, **63 failed / 2 passed (65)**. Every failure is `createRecoveryIncarnationService is not a function` / `createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort is not a function` — the expected missing-public-symbol failure, not a broken test file.

The 2 passing cases are deliberate and are the rail's anti-vacuity guards: they assert the generated matrices actually generated cases (`INVALID_REQUESTS.length === 21`, `ENTROPY_FAULTS.length === 7`, `KEY_FAULTS.length === 12`) and touch no missing symbol. A sweep that silently produced zero rows would fail these BEFORE any behaviour is asserted.

WHAT IS SPECIFIED (65 cases)
- Vocabulary: exactly three closed codes in precedence order, frozen; schema version literal; `RecoveryIncarnationErrorCode` and the result union pinned with `expectTypeOf` against the production constants.
- Request admission (21 rows + 2): every row asserts `calls.order` is EMPTY — the ordering claim is that nothing reached the CSPRNG, not merely that it refused. Covers missing/extra keys, the four forbidden caller-supplied identity fields (nonce, keyEpoch, counter, timestamp) plus incarnationRef, non-string/empty/over-long/control-char/non-NFC command IDs, and uppercase/63/65/non-hex/non-string digests. Accessor-backed request refused outright; a separate case mutates the request object AFTER `mint()` returns its promise and proves the binding still carries the pre-await snapshot.
- Real Node adapter path: full binding shape, every reference `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`, 128-hex Ed25519 signature, 88-hex (44-byte) SPKI, deep freeze; exactly 32 bytes requested from the CSPRNG; two commands over ONE generation get distinct incarnation ref, incarnation digest, key-epoch ref, key fingerprint and binding digest; identical retry does not remint (randomBytes called once); rebinding one command to a second generation refuses; two concurrent identical mints collapse to one minting.
- Fault matrix (19 rows): 7 entropy (throw, reject, non-Uint8Array, string, 31 bytes, 33 bytes, null) each asserting `generated === 0` so entropy is proven before a key exists; 12 key (throw, reject, null, wrong algorithm, non-Uint8Array SPKI, empty SPKI, non-object handle, sign throw, sign non-Uint8Array, verify throw, verify false, verify truthy-non-boolean) each asserting the CSPRNG was still asked for exactly 32. Every row goes through `expectRefusal`, which pins code AND layer `RECOVERY_INCARNATION` AND `truth: "UNKNOWN"` AND `authority: "NONE"` AND the absence of `binding`/`keyHandle`.
- Freshness proven on RAW material: a repeated CSPRNG block is refused even when BOTH the command and the generation differ — the derived reference would differ, so only a comparison on the raw block can catch it. Same shape for a repeated public key. Plus burning (a block reserved on an attempt that later died at the key leg is still refused later) and a simultaneous-claim case where exactly one of two concurrent commands may take a repeated block.
- Precedence: malformed + dead CSPRNG -> INPUT_INVALID with an empty call order; short entropy + dead key generation -> ENTROPY_UNAVAILABLE with `generated === 0`.
- Leak checks: a `SENTINEL` string is thrown from every one of the 19 fault legs and asserted absent from the serialized refusal. A recursive walker over `Reflect.ownKeys` (so NON-enumerable properties are included) forbids functions, Error, ArrayBuffer, any ArrayBuffer view, `CryptoKey`, the raw nonce hex, and any string matching /private|secret|pkcs8|seed/i. `keyHandle` is asserted non-enumerable and absent from `JSON.stringify`.
- Adapter-level protection: a fabricated `{}` handle and a `structuredClone` of a real handle both fail to sign, a destroyed handle stops signing, the handle serializes as `{}`, and the exported SPKI round-trips through `importKey`.

DELIBERATE TEST-DESIGN CHOICES WORTH REVIEWING
1. The stub port's DEFAULT legs are real WebCrypto Ed25519, not fakes; only the named fault row replaces a leg. A green row therefore cannot pass by never having touched real crypto.
2. Two cases recompute `sha256(domain || bytes)` independently and compare to the published digest. That is deliberate duplication of a one-line derivation, used as an oracle for "the raw block was hashed, not published" — it is not a reimplementation of the service's logic.
3. `expect(node instanceof webcrypto.CryptoKey)` rather than a name check, so a renamed class cannot slip through.

Node facts measured on THIS machine (v24.16.0), not assumed: `subtle.generateKey({name:'Ed25519'}, false, ['sign','verify'])` gives a private key with `extractable:false`, `type:'private'`, `usages:['sign']`; SPKI is 44 bytes; signatures are 64 bytes; verify succeeds. `@moe/store` is already a declared `@moe/daemon` dependency, so importing the digest TYPE adds no manifest change.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the recovery-incarnation contract and stateful mint service. Import only the type `BackupGenerationManifest['generationDigest']` from @moe/store; defensively snapshot the exact request synchronously before the first await and validate canonical NFC bounded command ID plus lowercase hex64 digest. Define immutable request/binding/proof/success/refusal/opaque-handle/crypto-port types, schema and error constants, fixed no-secret refusal factories, and domain-separated canonical hashing. Maintain per-service in-flight/success bindings by restore command so concurrent or repeated identical command+digest calls reuse one mint while rebinding the command to another generation refuses. Request exactly 32 entropy bytes, hash and reserve the raw block before any key await, refuse repeats independently of command context, then derive the context-bound incarnation reference; after key generation, fingerprint and reserve the complete canonical SPKI before self-proof, derive the key-epoch/binding digests, sign and verify the exact canonical challenge through the port, and return only a deep-frozen `MINTED`/authority-NONE result whose protected handle is frozen and non-enumerable. Same shape and same reason as the deviation on task-5606947a.

DESIGN POINTS THAT ARE LOAD-BEARING, NOT STYLE
- Freshness is proven on the RAW material, before any caller context is mixed in. `digestOf("nonce", entropy)` is compared and reserved before the key await; `digestOf("key", spki)` over the COMPLETE canonical SPKI, not a tail slice. A context-bound reference differs for every command id, so a comparison made after mixing in the command could never catch a CSPRNG that repeats — this ordering IS the guarantee.
- Reservation survives failure. The block is added to the seen set before the key leg, so an attempt that dies at key generation still burns its block. A block once exposed is never retried.
- Hash framing is domain-separated AND length-prefixed: `"<schema>:<domain>�"` then `"<len>:<value>�"` per part. Without framing, `("ab","c")` and `("a","bc")` collide, so a caller choosing a command id could steer one digest onto another binding's value.
- The request is snapshotted through `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors` ONCE, synchronously, before the first await; values are read out of the descriptors, never by a second property access. That is what makes accessor, proxy and mutate-during-await all one guard instead of three.
- Extra keys are REFUSED, not ignored. Silently dropping a caller-supplied `nonce`/`keyEpoch`/`counter`/`timestamp` would look to the caller like it had been honoured — the exact confusion the task rail forbids.
- Refusals are fixed module constants built by a factory that takes only a code and a literal reason. Nothing observed at a failure site can reach them, so no caught provider message, key byte or stack frame has a path into evidence even by accident.
- `attemptPort` returns a private `PORT_FAILED` symbol rather than rethrowing, so throw and reject collapse into one path and the diagnostic is dropped at the boundary.
- Verification is `verified !== true`, not falsiness, so a truthy non-boolean cannot pass for a signature check.
- One restore command mints at most once per process: identical retry returns the same binding, a concurrent identical call joins the same in-flight promise (registered synchronously before any await, so a same-tick second caller cannot start a second mint), and rebinding one command to a DIFFERENT generation refuses.

A REAL BUG FOUND IN MY OWN TEST FILE, worth flagging because it would have been invisible
`file(1)` reported the new test file as `data`, not source: three literal **NUL bytes** had landed inside string literals — one in the `"restore<NUL>command"` fixture and two in the `":nonce "` / `":key "` domain separators. Git would have classified the file as binary and served QA no diff at all (`mem:gotcha-literal-nul-in-source-makes-git-call-it-binary`). Fixed by rewriting each as an explicit `�` escape; `file(1)` now reports UTF-8 text and `tr -dc '\000' | wc -c` is 0 on every new file. I kept NUL as the framing separator rather than reverting to a space — it cannot occur in a hex digest or in an admitted command id, so it is the stronger separator; it just has to be spelled as an escape.
Second-order trap hit while fixing it: the Bash tool collapses `\\` in a single-quoted perl replacement, so `s/\x00/\\u0000/g` silently became perl's `\u` "uppercase next char" escape and emitted `0000` with the backslash eaten — a corrupted fix that still looked plausible. `s/\x00/chr(92)."u0000"/ge` avoids backslashes in the replacement entirely.

TEST CORRECTIONS made while implementing (both strengthen the suite):
- The `"a control character in the command id"` row genuinely carries U+0000, verified by `od -c`; a separate `"whitespace in the command id"` row was added because a space is not a control character and the two are different guards. Matrix count assertion moved 21 -> 22.
- The non-NFC row was verified at BYTE level to be decomposed (`r` + `\xcc\x81` = U+0301), so `normalize("NFC") === value` is the only guard that can reject it. Had it been the precomposed character, that row would have passed vacuously through the length or charset guard and proven nothing about NFC.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the production Node crypto adapter in a separate focused module. Use Node 24 WebCrypto/getRandomValues or randomBytes for the requested 32 bytes and `subtle.generateKey({name:'Ed25519'}, false, ['sign','verify'])`; require a private CryptoKey with type private, extractable false and signing usage, retain it only in a module-private WeakMap keyed by a frozen empty opaque handle, and export only the public key's canonical full SPKI DER. Re-import/round-trip the SPKI, require Ed25519 public metadata, implement Ed25519 sign and public verify for the service's challenge, and delete the handle on destroy; a structured clone or fabricated handle must not resolve to a key. Re-export only the reviewed `createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort` value from the public recovery-incarnation barrel, and add exact one-line bridges so the existing raw-Node bridge/loadability gate covers both modules.
implementationPlan.note:
Node crypto adapter + bridges landed. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0; focused suite **66/66 green, exit 0**.

ADAPTER
Private key is a non-extractable WebCrypto `CryptoKey`, never returned. Callers get `Object.freeze({})`; only this port's own WeakMap can turn one back into key material, so a fabricated `{}` or a `structuredClone` of a real handle is a different object identity and resolves to nothing. The WeakMap is PORT-private rather than module-private — a handle minted by one port cannot sign on another.
Every property the mint later depends on is ASSERTED, not assumed: `type === "private"`, `extractable === false`, `usages.includes("sign")`, `algorithm.name === "Ed25519"`, and the exported COMPLETE canonical SPKI DER is re-imported and required to come back as Ed25519 public metadata. A runtime that quietly handed back an extractable private key would otherwise satisfy every later step of the mint and nothing would notice.
Classic `KeyObject` was rejected deliberately, per the architect's note and confirmed: it is structured-cloneable and its PKCS8 bytes stay exportable while `JSON.stringify` yields `{}` — it LOOKS contained and is not.

HONEST LIMIT, stated in the module and worth QA's attention: non-extractable is protection against EXPORT, not durability. This key lives in process memory and dies with the process. It is not an OS-protected keystore reference, and nothing built on it may claim crash-resume until a durable protected provider exists.

TYPE FINDING (measured, not assumed): this package has no DOM lib, so `CryptoKey` is a runtime global but NOT a global type — `WeakMap<object, CryptoKey>` is a compile error. The type lives at `webcrypto.CryptoKey`. Separately, `subtle.generateKey` is typed to return one key OR a pair, so I narrowed with a real runtime shape guard (`isSigningPair`) rather than casting; the guard is not decoration, it is the only thing standing between a single-key return and a destructured `undefined`.

BRIDGES: three exact one-line bridges written and byte-verified (`od -c`) as `export * from "./<name>.ts";` + LF — `recovery-incarnation.js`, `recovery-incarnation.node.js`, `recovery-incarnation-contract.js`. `runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` computes the runtime tier as a forward closure, so all three modules are in it and a missing or wrong-content bridge fails there, not here (mem:gotcha-vitest-hides-missing-js-bridge).

Deliberately NOT published: `RECOVERY_ENTROPY_BYTES`, `RECOVERY_INCARNATION_LAYER`, the framing constant, `digestOf`, `snapshotRequest`, `isKeyPair`, `attemptPort`, the fixed refusal constants and every freshness set. TWO CASES ADDED THIS STEP, both aimed at DoD 2's "no counter, timestamp, backup byte or caller-selected ID can supply either fresh identity":
1. **Determinism**: two SEPARATE service instances — so neither carries the other's freshness memory — fed byte-identical entropy and key material produce byte-identical bindings. This is the case that would fail if a clock, counter or any ambient state had leaked into the derivation. Nothing else in the suite catches that; every other case varies the material.
2. Changing ONLY the backup generation moves incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, bindingDigest and the challenge digest together.

Together with the existing "repeated raw block refused even when BOTH command and generation differ" case, the two directions are now both pinned: context cannot mask repeated material, and material alone fully determines the binding.

CONSUMER EDGE — clause 1 is a LIMIT, not a claim. This lands the capability and no consumer edge. Nothing imports `createRecoveryIncarnationService` outside its own test. Named downstream daemon consumers, per the plan and architect-f39f0c46's comment-18289b05: **task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587** and **task-6f786c58cabf4f85be8ed4135e68a752** (plus task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683, the two-slot installer). implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review + mutation drill. Focused suite 72/72. One REAL defect found and fixed, and one drill that SURVIVED and exposed an untested direction.

DEFECT 1 — the port could be read twice and show two different public keys.
`prove` re-read `pair.publicKeySpki` at each use. A port answering with a GETTER shows one SPKI to the fingerprint and a different one to the published binding: both well-formed, signature verifies, binding looks complete, and its `verificationKeyFingerprint` covers bytes nobody ever receives. Written as a test FIRST and confirmed red before the fix — `expected '84de805d…' to be '22831cf5…'`, i.e. the fingerprint and the published hex genuinely disagreed. Fixed by `snapshotKeyMaterial`, which destructures every port-supplied property EXACTLY ONCE and copies the bytes. Also bounded the SPKI at 1024 bytes.

DEFECT 2 — the drill that survived, which is the more useful finding.
Neutralising the byte COPY (`Uint8Array.from(publicKeySpki)` -> `publicKeySpki`) left the suite fully GREEN. My getter test did not cover it: destructuring already reads the getter once, so the SINGLE READ is what fixes the getter case and the COPY defends a different attack — a port that mutates the array IN PLACE after handing it over. Exactly `mem:gotcha-redundant-operand-mutants-survive-inside-one-guard`: a guard that looks covered, whose direction the tests forgot. Fixed by adding the missing case, NOT by deleting the "redundant" copy: the stub now snapshots the SPKI it was HANDED at verify time, and the test mutates the shared array from inside `sign` (which runs after the fingerprint, before verify). Without the copy, one set of bytes is verified and a different set published — a binding whose signature covers a key nobody receives.

MUTATION DRILL — four arms, every restore byte-verified against the pre-drill SHA256, backups kept OUTSIDE the repo (these files are untracked, so `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` resolves nothing; see mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree).
- ARM 1 `seenNonceDigests.has(...)` -> false: 3 red — "refuses a repeated CSPRNG block even when the restore command differs", "burns a block seen on an attempt that later failed", "lets only one of two simultaneous commands claim a repeated block".
- ARM 2 `seenKeyFingerprints.has(...)` -> false: 1 red — "refuses a repeated public key even when the restore command differs".
- ARM 3 `verified !== true` -> false: 4 red — verification throws / returns false / returns a truthy non-boolean, plus "keeps the primary code when cleanup also fails".
- ARM 4 SPKI copy removed: SURVIVED at first (see defect 2), reddens after the fix with exactly "verifies the exact key bytes it publishes, even if the port mutates its array".
Every generated-case-count assertion (22 invalid requests, 7 entropy faults, 14 key faults) stayed GREEN in all four arms — the matrices never silently emptied. `recovery-incarnation.ts` restored to `1902069c…`, `recovery-incarnation-contract.ts` to `7dfd5a54…`, both confirmed byte-identical. No probe, drill or generated file remains: `git status` shows nothing matching drill/probe/scratch/.bak/.orig.

ALSO HARDENED: the signature is copied before verification for the same reason as the SPKI — the bytes verified must be the bytes published, and the port still holds a reference.

REVIEWED AND ACCEPTED, not silently ignored: `digestOf` length-frames STRING parts but appends byte parts raw. That is unambiguous today because a byte part is always the SOLE part of its call (`digestOf("nonce", entropy)`, `digestOf("key", spki)`) and both are fixed length. A future call mixing two byte parts would be ambiguous. I left the shape alone rather than churn the digest and the test oracles that pin its exact construction; the invariant is now stated in the code.

Every port call is wrapped in `attemptPort`, and the realistic unbounded input (an absurd SPKI) is now bounded, so I know of no reachable path — but the service is not wrapped in a blanket catch, because any blanket code choice would mislabel the failing stage.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use a stateful daemon mint service plus an injected protected-key crypto port. The default Node 24 adapter uses WebCrypto Ed25519 with a non-extractable private CryptoKey retained only in an adapter-private WeakMap; it returns a frozen empty opaque handle, canonical public SPKI metadata, and a self-verified binding proof. Rejected classic KeyObject because it is structured-cloneable and its private PKCS8 bytes remain exportable even though JSON.stringify misleadingly yields {}; rejected raw/private key bytes, PEM/PKCS8 outcomes, counter/time/restored-state derivation, caller nonce/key-epoch fields, and hashing only the backup/command. Raw 32-byte entropy fingerprints and full canonical SPKI fingerprints are compared and reserved independently before context-bound references are derived, so changing restoreCommandId or backupGenerationDigest cannot mask a repeated CSPRNG block or key. Add a distinct RECOVERY_INCARNATION_INPUT_INVALID code rather than mislabel malformed/hostile input as entropy or key failure. The service accepts the committed @moe/store BackupGenerationManifest['generationDigest'] type and validates lowercase hex64, but returns MINTED with authority NONE; it does not reimplement or claim BackupGeneration verification. RecoveryAnchor alone owns PREPARED/INSTALLED.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Re-measurement at committed HEAD c5c46bb7f10ecf3e72f5bcd4b9869858a0fdaeda found no recovery-incarnation mint, keyEpoch, entropy gate, protected-key port, or recovery key rotation under apps/packages; existing recoveryIncarnationRef occurrences are witness fields/validators only. The pinned design hash was recomputed as 1D9D1EC97D3F07247FBBC088045E0BA2FD6DA8307F10A9026C55106419383191. Hard dependency task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a is DONE with exit-zero store evidence (32 files/357 tests), and @moe/store now exports BackupGenerationManifest with generationDigest:string plus the real creation/verifier surfaces. Node 24.16 local probes proved subtle.generateKey({name:'Ed25519'}, false, ['sign','verify']) yields private extractable:false/public extractable:true, 44-byte SPKI, 64-byte signatures, successful Ed25519 verify, and InvalidAccessException on private PKCS8 export. apps/daemon/src/index.ts is 249 physical lines; add only compact reviewed exports and remove separator blank lines as needed to remain <=250. index-surface.test.ts pins the exact 32-value namespace and runtime-entrypoint.test.ts automatically requires an exact one-line .js bridge for every production .ts module. The task's downstream daemon consumers remain task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587 and task-6f786c58cabf4f85be8ed4135e68a752. @moe/store task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683 cannot import upward from apps/daemon; a later daemon restore controller must pass this structural binding/handle to the anchor rather than create a store->daemon dependency.
planningNotes.risks: A non-extractable WebCrypto CryptoKey hidden behind a WeakMap handle is protected against caller export but is process-volatile, not an OS-durable keystore reference. This task must state that limitation and must not claim crash-resume persistence or PREPARED authority; RecoveryAnchor/controller must later supply an OS-protected durable key provider before CORE-S14 can pass. Snapshot the exact request before the first await; reject proxies/accessors/extras and caller nonce/key/counter/time. Async simultaneous mints require atomic in-flight command binding plus synchronous reservation of raw entropy fingerprints before key generation and key fingerprints before proof verification; same command+digest reuses the in-process mint, while the same command rebound to another generation refuses. Burn suspect fingerprints even when later stages fail. Full SPKI DER, not a tail slice, is fingerprinted and round-tripped; sign/verify the canonical domain-separated binding challenge before returning. Every port throw/false/malformed value maps to a frozen constant refusal, cleanup failure never replaces the primary code, and no caught message/Error, Buffer/view, CryptoKey/KeyObject, function, raw nonce, or private-shaped field may escape. Keep both production sources <=250 and the root index <=250, preserve foreign work, and stage only the seven named paths.
